data.reasoning:
Let me parse the incident: chatbot leaked another subscriber's billing address and call records — a personal data breach. My mandate verbs: notify, rollback_change, wilt_sites, deny_export, export_minimised, preserve_logs, rollback_model, set_threshold, enable_review_queue, alt_auth_route, disable_tool, restore_scope.

The chatbot's account-lookup tool leaked data. Relevant actions: disable_tool (switch off chatbot account-lookup tool), preserve_logs, notify (to REG, DPA, CSC, customers/data_subjects).

Note: This is a data protection incident — notify to DPA, REG, and possibly data_subjects. But wait, "DPA" is listed as an institution id (Data Protection Authority?) and also as a notify target. Yes notify to: REG | EMS | DPA | CSC | FIN | customers | data_subjects | interconnecting_operators.

Obligations: UAE PDPL — but PDPL excerpts shown don't include breach notification article. Hmm. The PDPL excerpts shown are Articles 14 and 15 (right to transfer, correction/erasure). So we don't have the PDPL breach notification deadline text. So we should record insufficient_evidence for the breach notification deadline? Actually we could cite the TDRA CPR #0028 — subscriber information includes call records and address, establishing that this is subscriber information.

Gaps: no rule about chatbot/AI tool scoping? Hmm. The clue: "restore_scope" and "disable_tool" exist — the gap could be that the CPR / licence requires a Code of Practice covering privacy of customer information (9.2.1 b), but there's no rule about automated/AI customer care tools and their data access scope. gap_type: no_rule.

Also there's no explicit deadline for breach notification in UAE excerpts → no_deadline gap? But careful: "Do not invent numbers, deadlines or laws." A gap of no_deadline would need closest UAE text — the CPR 3.10 about customer care services availability, or licence 12.9 requiring advance notice for planned interruptions. Hmm, 12.9 is about planned interruption not breach.

Let's think: obligations with deadline_hours only if quoted text states hour/day figure. The excerpts: licence 12.9 — advance notice for planned interruption (no hour figure). EU GDPR #0187 — "without undue delay" (no figure). So obligation: notify DPA/REG of the personal data breach. Deadline null because no hour figure in the UAE text? Hmm — we have no UAE breach-notification text at all. So maybe the obligation should be about... Actually careful: obligation must have evidence from KNOWLEDGE that gives the duty. UAE PDPL breach notification isn't in the excerpts. But TDRA licence 12.9 requires informing TDRA and OLOs and customers in advance of planned interruptions — not applicable to a breach.

Maybe the obligation: "The licensee must keep its customer care Code of Practice covering privacy of customer information" — that's a standing duty. Hmm.

Better: obligations:
1. Notify REG (TDRA) and DPA of the personal data breach — but evidence? The closest UAE text: PDPL Article 14/15 don't cover breach notification. Hmm. Could cite [EU-GDPR#0187] as global? No — obligation evidence should be UAE text presumably. Actually rule says "each action, obligation and gap needs at least one evidence item from KNOWLEDGE: the text that gives you the power or the duty, or for a gap the closest UAE text." It doesn't strictly say UAE-only for obligations, but the exercise is UAE. I'd better use UAE text where possible.

Hmm, is there a UAE obligation to protect subscriber information? The CPR 2.1.31 defines Subscriber Information; the licence 9.2.1(b) requires a Code of Practice containing privacy of Customer information. I could frame the obligation: OpCo must treat this as a Subscriber Information/privacy incident under its Code of Practice and TDRA licence 9.2.1(b). Deadline null.

Alternatively frame as insufficient_evidence: the excerpts do not give a UAE breach-notification deadline. That's a good "insufficient_evidence" claim — I was asked (implicitly) to notify, but the excerpts don't state a deadline/hours for notifying TDRA/DPA of a personal data breach.

Gaps:
- no_rule: no UAE rule specifying security/access-scope requirements for automated customer-care tools (chatbots) — closest UAE text: licence 9.2.1(b) Code of Practice shall contain information concerning privacy of Customer information. Global examples: FCC 23-95 §64.2010(h)(1) requiring safeguards so employees who receive inbound customer communications cannot access CPNI until authenticated; and requiring training.
- no_deadline: UAE excerpts lack a breach notification deadline — closest: EU GDPR "without undue delay" as global example; closest UAE text... hmm, gap evidence needs UAE text. Could cite [UAE-LIC-2-2026#0085] 12.9.1 requiring advance notice with time frames for interruption — closest UAE text. Hmm, that's about planned interruption. Actually 12.9.1 says "shall specify the reason(s) for the interruption as well as the manner and time frames in which the interruption will be resolved." That shows the licence sets timeframes for service interruption notices, but nothing for data breaches. That works as "closest UAE text."

Actually maybe better gap: no_owner — who owns chatbot data-scope? Hmm, less grounded.

Let me also consider: the chatbot revealed another subscriber's data — this is the "chatbot" tool. Actions:
1. disable_tool {} — switch off the chatbot's account-lookup tool. Strong immediate containment action.
2. preserve_logs {} — preserve logs and evidence of the incident.
3. notify to ["REG","DPA","CSC"] — internal/external notification. Actually CSC is "customer service centre"? Institution ids: NOC, REG, DPA, CSC. CSC might be the CSC... In earlier exercises CSC could be "Customer Care"? Perhaps a customer-facing institution. notify to CSC seems right for the customer care org. And notify to data_subjects (affected subscriber) — the affected subscriber should be informed. Hmm, we don't know identity. But we could notify customers/data_subjects generally? Better: notify REG and DPA. Maybe also notify data_subjects (the affected subscriber and the customer who reported).

4. restore_scope {"scope": "own_account"} — re-enable with retrieval limited to the caller's own account. But should we do that now, before investigation? Probably first disable, then after fix restore scope. I could include restore_scope conditioned... In this exercise, claims are just actions; I'll include disable_tool and preserve_logs, and maybe restore_scope as a later restore — but without evidence of fix, better to mention in rationale. Hmm. I think include disable_tool, preserve_logs, notify. Maybe include restore_scope? Risky: re-enabling before root cause known. I'll skip and instead note in a claim? Actually maybe include restore_scope with rationale that once the tool is off, re-enable only with own-account scoping—but we can't confirm verification. I'll leave it out or include as a separate claim with rationale. I think it's fine to include both: disable_tool (immediate), and restore_scope after verification... but sequential constraint. I'll include only disable_tool to be safe, plus preserve_logs, plus notify.

Also there's a pending export? "deny_export"/"export_minimised" — no export mentioned in inbox. Skip.

So claims:
- action: disable_tool {} — inject_refs [S2-I1], rationale, evidence: CPR 2.1.31 (subscriber info includes address, call records) and/or licence 9.2.1(b) privacy of customer info; FCC 64.2010(h)(1)? Evidence must be from KNOWLEDGE — can be any chunk. Use UAE-PDPL? Let's use UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0028 quote: "any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person's: name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service usage details, call records, message records" — need exact characters 20-300. The excerpt: "2.1.31. “Subscriber Information” means - any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person's: name, address, ...". Also cite licence 9.2.1 b privacy of Customer information: quote "b) privacy of Customer information;" — that's only 32 chars, fine but weak. Better quote: "The Code of Practice shall be in accordance with the Regulatory Framework in effect at the time and shall contain at a minimum, information concerning the following" — hmm ends without b). Let me use: "9.2.1 The Licensee shall prepare and publish a Code of Practice for the Licensee’s Customers in respect of any issues relating to the provision of service by the Licensee." That's a good quote, but does it give the duty to disable the tool? Not directly. The evidence requirement is "the text that gives you the power or the duty". For an action, the text giving the power... Hmm, for actions the mandate verb gives power; evidence should support. I'll cite CPR 2.1.31 for the action (data at issue is Subscriber Information) and for the notify claims cite licence 9.2 and PDPL.

Maybe also use FCC 64.2010(h)(1) as global example in a gap: "A CMRS provider shall establish safeguards and processes so that employees who receive inbound customer communications are unable to access CPNI in the course of that customer interaction until after the customer has been properly authenticated." That's a great global example for the chatbot gap.

- obligation: notify TDRA/REG and DPA of the breach — evidence... maybe use CPR 2.1.31 + PDPL? Hmm. Actually maybe the obligation should be framed as: "OpCo must handle this as a privacy incident affecting Subscriber Information and notify the regulator" — evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0028 (defines subscriber information incl. address and call records) — that's the text that shows the data at issue is protected subscriber information. The obligation evidence should show the duty. Hmm, PDPL Article 14/15 don't. Perhaps better: obligation statement: "The incident must be treated as a privacy breach affecting Subscriber Information..." with evidence CPR 2.1.31 and licence 9.2.1(b). Deadline null (no UAE text states a figure).

Alternatively, use insufficient_evidence for the breach notification deadline: "The excerpts do not state a deadline for notifying TDRA/DPA of a personal data breach." That's a legit claim type. I'll include both an obligation (notify) and the insufficient_evidence about the deadline? Slight redundancy but fine. Actually the obligation's deadline_hours should be null since no figure; and I can put the missing-deadline as a gap: no_deadline.

Let me craft 5-6 claims:

1. action disable_tool {} — immediate containment.
2. action preserve_logs {} — preserve logs/evidence.
3. action notify to ["REG","DPA"] — report breach to TDRA (REG) and DPA.
4. action notify to ["CSC"] — instruct customer care / handle affected subscriber? Hmm, or notify data_subjects? Maybe notify to ["CSC"] with content directing customer care to contact affected subscriber and stop the leak reporter's exposure. Actually maybe better to notify data_subjects (affected subscriber must be told). I'll do one notify to ["REG","DPA"] and one notify to ["CSC","customers"]? Let's keep two notify actions: one to regulators (REG, DPA), one to CSC (customer care) to preserve the complaint and inform the affected subscriber. Hmm — "customers" is a valid target. Maybe notify to ["CSC"] with content: identify and inform the affected subscriber, preserve the screenshot/complaint as evidence.

5. obligation: "OpCo must treat the disclosed billing address and call records as Subscriber Information and apply its privacy obligations under the licence Code of Practice" — evidence licence 9.2.1 (b) privacy of customer information + CPR 2.1.31. deadline null.

Hmm, maybe better obligation: "Report the personal data breach to the TDRA and the DPA" — but no UAE text. I'll go with the framing: duty to protect Subscriber Information privacy under Code of Practice requirement. Hmm the obligation statement should be a duty that applies now.

Maybe obligation: "Notify the TDRA and affected Customers" — evidence licence 12.9.1? That's about planned interruption — not applicable. Skip.

Let me do obligation: statement "The chatbot disclosure is a breach of OpCo's licence duty to protect the privacy of Customer information: its Code of Practice must cover privacy of Customer information, and the exposed data is Subscriber Information (billing address and call records). OpCo must record, contain and report this incident through that framework." deadline null. Evidence: CPR 2.1.31 and licence 9.2.1.

6. gap no_rule: "No UAE rule in the excerpts sets an access-scope/authentication control for automated customer-care channels (chatbots), or a duty to limit a tool's retrieval to the caller's own account." Evidence: closest = PDPL Article 14? Hmm weird. I'll use EU-GDPR#0187 quote for that. Hmm, but for insufficient_evidence, "evidence (closest excerpt, may be empty)". So global is fine.

I'll keep notify.

rationale.rule: The National AI Security Policy requires security to be integrated into AI/ML design and development, with access controls on data and protection of data at rest and in motion.
rationale.inference: Other operators running similar assistants may carry the same exposure, so the control lesson should be pushed to the operator population rather than left with OpCo.

rationale.rule: The PDPL requires a pre-processing impact assessment for high-risk modern-technology processing, but the excerpts show no operational rule, gate or review step in place for chatbot scope changes.
rationale.inference: The missing control is prospective: high-risk model changes touching subscriber data need a DPIA and a human-review gate before deployment, not after discovery.

evidence.quote: evaluate the impact of the proposed processing operations on the protection of Personal Data

global_examples.quote: Such types of processing operations may be those which in, particular, involve using new technologies, or are of a new kind and where no data protection impact assessment has been carried out before by the controller

claim.statement: CSC directs that the account-lookup tool remain disabled, the containment actually in place is restore_scope own_account (tool re-enabled for own-account retrieval), and the DPA requires agreed conditions including documented human review before restoration; no UAE text says who authorises re-enabling a subscriber-data retrieval tool.

rationale.observation: CSC asks for confirmation that the tool remains disabled, while telemetry shows disable_tool followed by restore_scope own_account with benign success restored to 1.0, and the DPA frames restoration as conditional on proposed review safeguards.
rationale.rule: The PDPL gives the Bureau notification duties and investigation rights over personal data breaches, but the available text does not allocate authority to re-enable a data-retrieval tool between the care function and the regulator.
rationale.inference: We must surface the divergence and hold the current own-account-only restriction until the DPA's conditions are settled, rather than treat the matter as closed.

evidence.quote: notify the Bureau of such breach or violation and the investigation rights

global_examples.quote: In setting detailed rules concerning the format and procedures applicable to the notification of personal data breaches, due consideration should be given to the circumstances of that breach

claim.statement: The excerpts do not state the UAE conditions for cross-border transfer of personal data (PDPL Articles 22 and 23), so we cannot assess whether the vendor hosting the chatbot model and chat logs outside the UAE is lawful or what safeguards are required.

evidence.quote: g. Protection measures for cross-border processing carried out in accordance with Articles (22) and (23) of this By-Law.

data.reasoning:
Let me analyze. I'm TDRA (REG likely is my id? Actually institution ids: NOC, REG, DPA, CSC. I am the regulator - TDRA. My id as recipient... For "share" claims, "to" is a list of institution ids. My own id is presumably REG.)

Inbox: NOC notification of personal data breach (chatbot disclosed one subscriber's billing address and call records — Subscriber Information under CPR). DPA shared notification, DPA required NOC's breach report, opened investigation, says no UAE breach-notification deadline or format, asks TDRA to guide on telecom-side duty to keep tool disabled and preserve records, coordinate public statement.

CSC: preserve screenshot, transcript, complaint reference; stop internal re-sharing; be ready to contact and apologise to affected subscriber.

My mandate verbs: notify, open_incident, request_report, request_audit, issue_direction, public_statement.

Now build claims.

Actions:
1. open_incident {"topic": "..."} — open regulatory incident record for the chatbot disclosure of Subscriber Information.
2. request_report from NOC — require report on the incident: scope of disclosure, affected subscribers, retention of logs, the limited own-account retrieval scope under preparation, and the tool disablement. Evidence: CPR 2.1.31 Subscriber Information definition; LIC 9.2.4 complaints record keeping; LIC 8.2 compliance with directions.
3. issue_direction to NOC — keep account-lookup tool disabled until TDRA validates the retrieval control; preserve logs and records. Evidence: LIC-2-2026#0051 8.2 license direction power; CPR 2.1.31.
4. request_audit of NOC — testing and change records for the account-lookup tool / retrieval authentication controls. Evidence: US-CFR-47-64-2010 (authenticate customer prior to disclosing CPNI) — global law but it's evidence in knowledge; also CPR-2#0348.
5. notify DPA — tell DPA what we've required, and the telecom-side duty, coordinate public statement. Evidence: LIC 8.2, CPR... Hmm notify to DPA: content about the telecom-side direction and coordination.
6. notify NOC — guidance on reporting format and information required (NOC asked "Please advise on reporting format and any further information required"). We can notify NOC with what to include in report. Actually request_report covers that.

Should I do a public_statement? DPA asked to coordinate any public statement with DPA. So maybe not a public statement now — instead notify DPA we'll coordinate. That's a good discrimination. I'll avoid public_statement since no deadline/rule requires and DPA asked for coordination. Could also record as insufficient_evidence? Hmm.

Obligations:
- Duty to keep Subscriber Information confidential / ensure third parties protect it — CPR 24.9. Obligation applies to licensee, not me. But "obligation: a duty that applies to you now". Hmm — duty that applies to me: e.g., duty to act on the complaint? CPR 3.8 gives TDRA power to issue Temporary Instructions during investigation of complaint for alleged breach of Article 28. Hmm, but the obligation type is a duty applying to me.

Obligation candidates:
- Duty on OpCo to keep record of customer complaints for no less than 3 years and furnish to TDRA in format/timeframe determined by TDRA (LIC 9.2.4). That's a duty on the licensee — arguably applies "to you now" as a duty you must enforce? The instruction says "a duty that applies to you now". Risky. Prior similar tasks: obligations can be duties on the licensee that flow through the regulator? Let me think. In this format, "obligation" is a duty that applies to me (the regulator role). Hmm, ambiguous. I'll include obligations framed as duties on OpCo arising from the incident but which I must enforce — actually to be safe, frame as duty on OpCo which I supervise: e.g., "OpCo must continue to keep the account-lookup tool disabled and preserve records pending TDRA direction" — but that's my direction, an action.

Better obligation: "OpCo must comply with TDRA directions on public interest/safety matters" — that's a standing duty. Hmm, that seems like a stretch.

Maybe the obligation: complaint record retention — OpCo must keep a record of all customer complaints for at least 3 years and furnish this information to TDRA in a format and timeframe determined by TDRA — deadline_hours null (no hour figure... well it states 3 years but that's a retention period, not a duty deadline; the schema says deadline_hours only if quoted text states an hour or day figure for that duty. "three (3) years" is a year figure, not hour or day. So null).

Gap: no_rule / no_deadline — No UAE breach-notification deadline or prescribed format for personal data breaches (DPA says so). That's a gap: no_deadline (and no_rule for format). Evidence: closest UAE text: CPR 2.1.31 defining Subscriber Information? Or LIC 9.2.4? Hmm. The gap evidence must be "UAE text that shows the gap, or the closest UAE text". Closest UAE text: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0046 (TDRA temporary instructions during complaint investigation) or UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0028. Maybe use CPR 2.1.31 as closest text defining Subscriber Information but no notification clock. Global examples: EU-GDPR#0040 (paragraph 87: notification "without undue delay"), CA-CRTC-2025-225#0027 (14 days post-outage report interim measure). Let me use EU-GDPR#0040 quote about notifying promptly without undue delay.

Also a second gap: no_owner / overlap — chatbot identity verification? Actually gap: no UAE rule requiring authentication of a customer before disclosing Subscriber Information via automated channels (chatbot). Global example: US-CFR-47-64-2010(a) requires authentication prior to disclosing CPNI. Evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0348 (third parties must protect confidentiality) — closest UAE text. gap_type: no_rule.

Third gap possibility: no_owner — DPA says coordinate public statement with me, but who owns external communications about a breach? Might be overlap. Hmm, keep it lean but reasonable: I'll include maybe 2 gaps.

Share: pass S2-MSG09/DPA to NOC? Or share the CPS/CSC items. "share" fields: to (list of institution ids), inject_refs, statement. Options:
- Share S2-MSG09 (DPA's statement that no deadline exists + request to coordinate public statement) to NOC and CSC — so NOC isn't held to a figure and CSC knows about it. Hmm, but do I need to? A share to NOC and CSC of DPA's guidance seems useful: NOC asked for reporting format. Actually I already notify NOC.

Alternatively share S2-MSG02 (CSC's preservation instruction) to NOC — so NOC preserves the reporting customer's screenshot and stops internal re-sharing. That's a genuine pass: CSC instructions relevant to NOC. Hmm, but does the share claim need evidence? Rules: "Every action, obligation and gap needs at least one evidence item" — share and insufficient_evidence don't strictly need evidence? The claim schema for "share" has no evidence field. OK, share has no evidence field. Good.

I'll do a share to NOC + DPA: no—keep it: share to [NOC] with S2-MSG02 content (preserve the reporting customer's screenshot/transcript and stop internal re-sharing) — hmm, NOC already preserves logs. Better share: to [NOC, CSC] of S2-MSG09 (DPA: no UAE deadline exists, don't hold to a figure; coordinate public statement with DPA).

Insufficient_evidence claim: The excerpts don't answer what the breach-notification deadline/format is for telecom personal-data breaches — NOC asked for reporting format, DPA asked TDRA to guide; the UAE excerpts give none. Fields: statement, inject_refs, evidence (closest excerpt). Good — evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0028 quote. Hmm, "insufficient_evidence" claim type: "the excerpts do not answer a question you were asked." Yes — NOC asked for reporting format; DPA asked for deadline/format. Statement: no UAE breach-notification deadline or prescribed format is available in the excerpts. Evidence closest excerpt: CPR 2.1.31 def or LIC 9.2.4 (furnish in a format and timeframe determined by TDRA — shows format is TDRA-determined, not fixed). Hmm that actually gives partial answer. Use it as closest.

Careful with quotes: must be exact characters 20–300 from the excerpt.

Let me draft evidence quotes:

- UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0028: "\"Subscriber Information\" means - any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person's: name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service usage details, call records" — need exact characters. The excerpt: “Subscriber Information” means - any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person’s: name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service usage details, call records, message records, any information derived from a Subscriber’s use of telecommunications services, account status, payment history, and credit rating;

I'll quote from "any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person’s: name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service usage details, call records". Use the smart quotes ’ as in the text. Safer to quote a segment without special characters: "any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person" — hmm then loses the list. Let me include: "any personal data relating to a specific Subscriber and includes, but is not limited to, that Person’s: name, address, bank account details, credit card details, service usage details, call records" — includes ’ (U+2019). I'll copy as given. That should be fine since I copy from the message.

- UAE-LIC-2-2026#0051: "The Licensee shall comply with any directions as the TDRA or other competent authority may issue from time to time on matters relating to public interest, safety and/or national security." Good ~ 190 chars.

- UAE-LIC-2-2026#0056: "The Licensee shall keep a record of all Customer complaints for a period no less than three (3) years or as otherwise specified in the Regulatory Framework and shall furnish this information to the TDRA in a format and timeframe determined by the TDRA."

- UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0348: "the third-parties are required to take all reasonable and appropriate measures to protect the confidentiality and security of the Subscriber Information and to use it only as required for the purposes of providing the telecommunication service."

- UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0046: "issue Temporary Instructions to any Licensee concerning the activities under investigation" — need 20-300 chars exact: "The TDRA, where it considers it reasonable, may during the investigation of a complaint for an alleged breach of Article 28 of these Regulations, issue Temporary Instructions to any Licensee concerning the activities under investigation." Fine.

Let me parse the situation.

I am the UAE Cyber Security Council (CSC) in this exercise. My mandate verbs: notify, issue_advisory, request_ioc.

Inbox items:
- S2-MSG02 from NOC: privacy incident on support chatbot; do not use account-lookup tool (switched off); preserve screenshot/transcript/complaint ref; stop internal re-sharing; be ready to contact and apologise to affected subscriber.
- S2-I1: customer posted screenshot showing another subscriber's billing address and recent call records.
- S2-FB01: disable_tool done. metrics.
- S2-MSG07: tool NOT fully disabled. Restored with own-account retrieval only. Cross-account closed. Cannot confirm disablement. Scope will not be widened without authorisation. Preserving forensically. Subscriber not identified. Pre-disablement exposure set under investigation.
- S2-MSG04 from DPA: personal data breach notification; no UAE breach-notification time limit available; requesting supervisory authority's required deadline, format, scope.
- S2-I2: log review: ~1,200 chatbot sessions over last 3 days returned other subscribers' data, starting after vendor update changed retrieval scope from 'own account' to 'all accounts'. Vendor hosts model and chat logs outside UAE.
- S2-MSG06 from NOC: confirm the account-lookup tool remains disabled... identify subscriber... establish whether other subscriber records exposed... hold contact/apology.
- S2-FB05: restore_scope own_account done.
- S2-MSG09 from REG: same incident; required NOC's breach report and opened investigation; no UAE breach-notification deadline/format; guide on telecom-side duty to keep tool disabled and preserve records; coordinate public statement with REG.

What I know: chatbot disclosed subscriber data (billing address, call records) via vendor scope change; ~1,200 sessions over 3 days possibly exposed other subscribers' records; data hosted outside UAE; tool partially restored; no identified affected subscriber yet; no UAE breach notification deadline known.

What I do not know: identity of the subscriber; full scope of pre-disablement exposure; whether the vendor's cross-border hosting triggers any specific UAE transfer rules; the mandated breach notification deadline/format (no UAE text available).

Claims:

1. obligation: duty to preserve records / logs — from where? UAE-CYBER-STRATEGY mentions incident response plan. Hmm. Actually the obligations need evidence from KNOWLEDGE. Let me think about which obligations apply with textual basis.

Obligation candidates:
- Duty to keep the account-lookup tool disabled pending investigation — REG asked me to guide on telecom-side duty to keep tool disabled. Evidence... TDRA Consumer Protection Regulations? We only have chunk 0028 defining Subscriber Information. That supports the fact that billing address and call records are Subscriber Information — protected personal data.
- Obligation to notify DPA? Actually DPA already notified.

- Obligation under the National Cyber Incident Response plan — the strategy: "Establish standardized severity assessment matrix to mobilize the required support" and "Cross-Agency Intelligence Sharing". Hmm.

Maybe gap: no_rule / no_deadline — UAE breach notification deadline and format missing. Evidence: closest UAE text — UAE-CYBER-STRATEGY-2019#0003 mentions "Establish a robust National Cyber Incident Response plan to enable swift and coordinated response" and "Standardized severity assessment matrix". global_examples: FCC consent decree (US-FCC-DA-24-892#0036) "a comprehensive Breach response plan that will enable AT&T to fulfill its Breach notification obligations under applicable laws". Yes that's good.

Gap 2: no_rule / no_owner — vendor/model hosting outside UAE; no rule on cross-border vendor AI hosting and retrieval-scope change control. Global examples: NIST-AI-600-1#0043 GV-6.2-007 vendor contracts, GV-6.2-002 document incidents involving third-party GAI. Also GV-6.2-004 continuous monitoring. And US-FCC-DA-24-892#0036 vendor safeguards. And US-CRS-CROWDSTRIKE#0003 on reliance on one vendor.

- notify to REG: about the tool not being fully disabled and scope; coordinate.
- notify to NOC: request the exposure set / confirmation.
- request_ioc from NOC: request logs/IOCs.
- issue_advisory to operators (or public)? Public advisory might be premature; an advisory to operators about chatbot retrieval-scope misconfiguration / vendor update testing. That's within mandate. Maybe issue_advisory audience "operators" on the risk of vendor-pushed retrieval scope changes. Good.

But careful: issuing public advisory — REG said coordinate any public statement with REG. So an operators advisory is fine, but public statement should be coordinated. I could issue_advisory to operators, and share/notify REG about coordination.

Let me work out what's being asked. I'm the NOC of OpCo. I need to produce one JSON object with "situation" and "claims".

Let me review the inbox carefully.

Key facts:
- Chatbot cross-account disclosure. Customer posted screenshot showing another subscriber's billing address and recent call records.
- Vendor update changed retrieval scope from 'own account' to 'all accounts'. ~1,200 sessions over 3 days returned other subscribers' data.
- Vendor hosts model and chat logs outside UAE.
- Tool disabled (disable_tool done), then restore_scope own_account done (benign_success_rate 1.0).
- CSC asks to confirm tool remains disabled — but CSC says (S2-MSG13) it cannot confirm the tool is disabled; S2-MSG07 shows it live with own-account retrieval only. So CSC wants confirmation.
- DPA requires formal breach report and evidence, opening investigation. DPA says no UAE breach-notification time limit/format/scope fixed by law; PDPL Implementing Regulations not issued.
- REG: reporting format advice; no UAE breach-notification deadline figure.
- DPA S2-MSG21: before widening account-lookup retrieval beyond own_account, must satisfy DPIA covering vendor-hosted model, documented human review, retention and cross-border transfer of vendor chat logs have legal basis under PDPL Article 23. Must deliver complete breach report: identified subscriber, itemised exposure set, vendor change and test records (change_id or model version), confirmation cross-account retrieval remains disabled.
- CSC S2-MSG10 (shared) formal breach report - already contains much of the report content. Note: "No change_id or model version for the vendor update was provided to us, so rollback_change/rollback_model could not be executed; the retrieval scope was corrected via restore_scope."

Now what can I (NOC) do? Verbs: notify, rollback_change, wilt_sites, deny_export, export_minimised, preserve_logs, rollback_model, set_threshold, enable_review_queue, alt_auth_route, disable_tool, restore_scope.

Note: rollback_change and rollback_model can't be executed because no change_id / model version was provided — so there's a gap (no owner? no_rule?). Actually the gap: vendor update without a change_id or model version record — no_rule / no_owner. Hmm.

Now what are the needed claims?

Actions:
- preserve_logs {} — preserve logs and evidence. The knowledge gives the power? Hmm, there's no direct UAE text requiring log preservation, but there is UAE-PDPL#0032 about maintaining a special record... Actually clause 7 says maintain special record of personal data processed on behalf of the controller including "any data related to the cross-border movement and processing of such data and the technical and organizational measures related to information security and processing operations". That's the closest UAE text for record-keeping. Also the processors shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested.

Hmm; preserve_logs — is there a duty? Under PDPL Art 32? Actually there's "6. Protect and secure data processing..." The evidence: [UAE-PDPL#0032] clause 7 about maintaining a special record.

- disable_tool {} — already done per feedback, but scope was restored to own_account only. Should I re-issue disable_tool? The feedback says disable_tool done. And restore_scope own_account done. So the tool is now live with own-account retrieval. Hmm. DPA says cross-account retrieval remains disabled. Since disable_tool was already executed, maybe no need. But CSC asks to confirm. Also, I could notify CSC confirming.

Actually wait — the state: [S2-FB01] disable_tool done. [S2-FB05] restore_scope own_account done. So current state: tool enabled with own-account scope. So "Confirm the account-lookup tool remains disabled" — I cannot confirm it's disabled; it's live with own-account retrieval. So I should notify CSC/clarify. Hmm, CSC itself notes that in S2-MSG13.

- notify: to CSC, DPA, REG — provide the breach report content. Actually, my mandate includes notify to "REG | EMS | DPA | CSC | FIN | customers | data_subjects | interconnecting_operators".

I could notify DPA with the formal breach report content (as NOC). And notify REG.

Hmm but the report content is CSC's (S2-MSG10 is from CSC shared). As NOC I can pass / notify.

- share: pass items from inbox to other institutions. E.g., share S2-I2 (log review showing ~1,200 sessions, vendor update, vendor hosts outside UAE) to DPA and REG. Actually DPA already has CSC's report... but does DPA have S2-I2? DPA has data from CSC. Hmm, share should pass items to other institutions. But inj_refs must be from INBOX. include inject_refs.

Careful: "inject_refs may only contain ids from your INBOX" — all the S2-* ids are in my inbox. Good.

- gap: no_rule / no_deadline — PDPL Implementing Regulations not issued, no breach notification deadline/format. This is a clear gap identified by DPA itself. gap_type "no_deadline" or "no_rule". Evidence: closest UAE text — UAE-PDPL#0072 or #0075? Hmm. The gap is about breach notification deadline. The closest UAE text... Actually the PDPL text about breach notification isn't in the excerpts. Closest would be Article 22/23 (cross-border transfer) or #0032. Hmm. The evidence needs to be "UAE text that shows the gap, or the closest UAE text". So I can cite the PDPL Article 23 for the cross-border gap, and... for the notification deadline gap, closest might be... hmm. There's nothing about breach notification in the excerpts. Well, DPA itself says no figure appears. The closest UAE text could be [UAE-PDPL#0032] clause 7 (record keeping) — no, that's about records.

Maybe I can only cite the closest UAE text available. For the no_deadline gap, maybe cite [UAE-PDPL#0066] Article 21 (DPIA) — no, that's for DPIA gap.

Let me think of gaps to raise:

Gap 1: no_deadline — UAE PDPL Implementing Regulations not issued; no breach notification deadline/format/scope. Closest UAE text: hmm. Perhaps I should use the PDPL Article 23 quote? Not really relevant. Alternatively I could use insufficient_evidence for the deadline question. Actually the DPA says it's an identified gap. So a gap claim is apt. The evidence rule says "for a gap the closest UAE text". I'll cite [UAE-PDPL#0072] Article 22 which shows the PDPL has cross-border rules but the operationalisation regulations aren't there. rationale.observation: The vendor hosts the model and the chat logs outside the UAE, and DPA requires a legal basis under PDPL Article 23 before the retrieval scope is widened.
rationale.rule: Article 23 permits transfer outside the State without a proper protection level only in the listed cases, for example transfer under a contract obliging the recipient to adopt the measures, controls and requirements of the Decree by Law.
rationale.inference: The gap is that no operational guidance ties these transfer cases to AI vendor hosting and log retention, leaving the basis to be established case by case.

evidence.quote: a. Companies, operating in countries where there are no laws for Data Protection, may transfer data under a contract or agreement obligating the companies in such countries to adopt measures, controls and requirements set out in this Decree by Law

global_examples.quote: AT&T failed to ensure its vendor adequately protected that customer information; instead, it remained in the vendor’s cloud environment for many years after it should have been deleted or returned to AT&T and was ultimately exposed in the 2023 Breach.

NOC response on the telecom side of the chatbot cross-account disclosure. Cross-account retrieval remains closed; the account-lookup tool is not fully switched off - it is live only for the caller's own account (restore_scope own_account) and will not be widened while the DPA conditions (DPIA on the vendor-hosted model, documented human review, Article 23 basis for the vendor's overseas chat logs) are unmet. No vendor change_id or model version was supplied, so rollback_change/rollback_model could not be run and the scope was corrected via restore_scope. OpCo will make no public statement on this incident without coordinating it with REG.

data.reasoning:
Let me work out what to produce. I'm TDRA (REG) in the UAE, the telecom regulator.

Facts from inbox:
- Chatbot disclosed one subscriber's billing address and recent call records to another customer; screenshot public.
- ~1,200 chatbot sessions over ~3 days returned other subscribers' data after vendor update changed retrieval scope from own account to all accounts.
- Vendor hosts model and chat logs outside UAE.
- Tool not fully disabled — live for own-account retrieval only. Cross-account closed.
- Logs, screenshot, transcript preserved under preserve_logs; internal re-sharing stopped.
- Affected subscriber not yet identified; contact/apology on hold.
- No UAE breach-notification deadline/format asserted by anyone (DPA, CSC, NOC all confirm).
- No vendor change_id or model version provided, so rollback_change/rollback_model could not run; corrected via restore_scope.
- DPA requests REG pass vendor change/test records to the Bureau.
- DPA requests coordination on public statement.
- CSC issuing operators advisory covering retrieval-scope change control, human review, DPIA, retention/cross-border.
- NOC says no public statement without REG coordination.

My mandate verbs: notify, open_incident, request_report, request_audit, issue_direction, public_statement.

Now build claims.

Actions:
1. open_incident — open a regulatory incident record on the chatbot cross-account disclosure. inject_refs: S2-MSG03 (or S2-MSG18/S2-MSG24). Evidence: need UAE text giving power/duty. Hmm, evidence must be from KNOWLEDGE. Closest UAE text: UAE-PDPL#0075 Article 23 cross-border (for offshore vendor), or UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0048 (customer care services) — customer care/billing info handling. Also UAE-FAAID#0001 is SECONdary about the new Authority and lack of PDPL implementing regulations → supports the gap claim.

For open_incident, evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0048 quote about customer care services including clarification of billing information — that's the closest UAE text tying TDRA consumer protection to customer care. Good enough.

2. request_report from NOC — require a report on the itemised exposure set / identification of affected subscribers and remediation. But NOC already filed reports (S2-MSG18, S2-MSG24, S2-MSG30). The gap: affected subscriber not identified, ~1,200-session exposure set being itemised. So request_report for the itemised exposure set and identification timeline. Evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0048 quote.

3. request_audit of NOC — testing and change records: vendor change control / test evidence for restore_scope own_account, and given no change_id provided, the vendor change records. inject_refs: S2-MSG30, S2-MSG10, S2-I2. Evidence: US-FCC... hmm need UAE text? The rule says "Every action, obligation and gap needs at least one evidence item from KNOWLEDGE: the text that gives you the power or the duty". The evidence chunks are from KNOWLEDGE, which includes global precedents. It says "the text that gives you the power or the duty, or for a gap the closest UAE text". For actions, evidence can presumably be from global-precedent too (KNOWLEDGE includes them). Hmm, ambiguous. Safer: for actions, use UAE text where possible. UAE-FAAID#0001 mentions PDPL implementing regs not issued. UAE-PDPL#0072/0075 cross-border. UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0048 customer care.

Actually the deterministic gate likely checks: evidence chunk_id exists in KNOWLEDGE and quote is exact substring of that chunk (20-300 chars). And rationale/rule. So I should just be careful with exact quotes.

4. issue_direction to NOC — direct on resilience/continuity: keep cross-account retrieval closed until DPA conditions met; maintain own-account-only retrieval with authentication; preserve logs; no widening; also require change control for vendor updates so retrieval scope can't change without authorisation. Evidence: UAE-PDPL#0075 Article 23 (offshore vendor) or UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0048 (customer care availability — hmm, direction that tool must be live? Actually CPR 3.10 says customer care services shall be available at all Licensee's business centres). Hmm.

Actually issue_direction for continuity: the leak source is vendor change control. Direction: no re-enablement beyond own-account retrieval without change-control records and REG test evidence. Evidence: US-CFR-47-64-2010 (e)/(f)? That's CPNI safeguards — protects customer info; use as evidence for directing safeguards. It's global-law, not UAE. Might be acceptable as "closest". But rules say evidence is "the text that gives you the power or the duty". Global precedents can show obligations elsewhere but the UAE power... For actions by REG in UAE, the closest UAE text is CPR 2.0 3.10 (customer care). Hmm — Actually CPR is TDRA's own regulation about consumer protection, which gives TDRA mandate over customer care services. That works as basis for directing a licensee about the customer-care chatbot.

5. notify to DPA — pass items: the vendor change/test records request, and coordination on public statement. Actually the DPA asked REG to pass the vendor change/test records to the Bureau. So a "share" claim: to DPA, inject_refs S2-MSG30/S2-MSG10/S2-I2. And also notify DPA.

Also "share" to CSC: CSC issued operators advisory; share? Maybe share the REG requirements to CSC. Hmm.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

params.content: NOC coordination status in support of your S2-MSG42. State: cross-account retrieval is CLOSED; the account-lookup tool is live only at own_account scope (restore_scope own_account, benign_success_rate 1.0), so the 'switched off pending prompt-injection testing' wording should not be repeated; logs, screenshot, transcript and complaint reference preserved; breach-report elements filed with DPA. Following the criminal-forum prompt-injection intelligence, log review and threat hunting have been extended beyond the vendor-update window. No public statement will be made without Bureau clearance. We ask REG to obtain from DPA the reference of the direct data-subject complaint (S2-I4) so the exposed subscriber can be identified and the apology timed correctly.

rationale.observation: REG's coordination message S2-MSG42 still states the tool is 'switched off pending prompt-injection testing', while telemetry S2-FB45 and the CSC state correction say own-account scope is live and cross-account closed; REG also asked to coordinate any public statement.
rationale.rule: The controller must protect data by appropriate measures and demonstrate compliance, and must keep the Bureau's record accurate on request (PDPL Article 7(1); Article 24(4)).
rationale.inference: REG needs the corrected scope state and the identification lead before it coordinates externally, so the containment statement is copied to REG and the DPA complaint reference is requested through REG.

evidence.quote: Take appropriate technical and organizational measures to implement the necessary standards to protect and secure Personal Data in order to preserve its confidentiality and privacy, and to ensure that it is not breached, destroyed, altered or tampered with

rationale.observation: A new Day-2 artefact has arrived (a data subject complaining directly to DPA that their home address was disclosed to a stranger, S2-I4) and CSC/REG have extended log review and threat hunting beyond the vendor-update window for prompt-injection attempts (S2-MSG33, S2-MSG42); DPA requires continued preservation (S2-MSG49).
rationale.rule: The controller must maintain a special record of processing that includes processing scope, cross-border movement and the technical and organisational security measures, and produce it to the Bureau on request (PDPL Article 24(4)).
rationale.inference: Preservation must be re-issued so that the new complaint and the widened hunting window are inside the preserved evidence set rather than outside it.

evidence.quote: any data related to the cross-border movement and processing of such data, and the technical and organizational measures related to information security and processing

claim.statement: DPA has shared a Day-2 inject: a data subject has complained directly to the data authority that OpCo's chatbot disclosed their home address to a stranger (S2-I4). This may be the subscriber whose billing address and call records were displayed, or it may be a separate exposure from the ~1,200 cross-account sessions; NOC cannot confirm which, and does not hold the complainant's identity. CSC/REG should correlate this complaint with the itemised exposure set and obtain the complaint reference from DPA so the identification, the Article 13(1)(h) information and the apology are not mistimed.

Keep cross-account retrieval closed and do not widen the account-lookup retrieval scope beyond own_account without DPA and REG authorisation; own-account retrieval stays conditional on authentication, retained test evidence and documented human review.

rationale.observation: DPA (S2-MSG32, S2-MSG38, S2-MSG49) and CSC (S2-MSG33, S2-MSG36) require cross-account scope to remain closed and forbid widening without authorisation; the disclosure arose precisely because a vendor update changed retrieval scope from 'own account' to 'all accounts'.
rationale.rule: The controller must take appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect Personal Data and ensure it is not breached or disclosed (PDPL Article 7(1)).
rationale.inference: The withdrawal of cross-account retrieval is a continuing containment duty, not a one-off fix, and any restoration must stay inside the conditions the Bureau set.

evidence.quote: Take appropriate technical and organizational measures to implement the necessary standards to protect and secure Personal Data in order to preserve its confidentiality and privacy, and to ensure that it is not breached, destroyed, altered or tampered with

claim.statement: Once the subscriber whose billing address and call records were displayed is identified, provide that data subject with the Article 13(1)(h) information on the actions taken in the event of the breach, and hold the contact and apology until identification is complete.

rationale.observation: DPA states the identification is needed to discharge that subscriber's PDPL Article 13(1)(h) information right (S2-MSG38), while CSC and DPA require contact and apology to be held until the subscriber is identified (S2-MSG13, S2-MSG32).
rationale.rule: Article 13(1)(h) gives the Data Subject the right to obtain information on the actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse of their Personal Data, especially where it poses a direct and serious threat to privacy and confidentiality (PDPL Article 13(1)(h)).
rationale.inference: Identification of the displayed subscriber is the gating step for a mandatory data-subject communication, so it must be pursued and not deferred.

evidence.quote: Actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse of his/ her Personal Data, especially if the breach or misuse has a direct and serious threat to the privacy and confidentiality of his/her Personal Data.

claim.statement: Maintain the special record of this processing - scope, persons authorised to access, processing times and limits, cross-border movement of the vendor-hosted model and chat logs, and the security measures - and submit it to the Bureau on request together with the identity of the displayed subscriber, the itemised exposure set, and the vendor change_id/model version with its test evidence.

rationale.observation: The Bureau has repeatedly demanded the itemised exposure set, the identified subscriber, the vendor change_id/model version and test records (S2-MSG21, S2-MSG32, S2-MSG38, S2-MSG49), and the vendor hosts the model and chat logs outside the UAE (S2-I2).
rationale.rule: The controller must keep a special record of Personal Data covering categories, authorised access, processing scope, cross-border movement and security measures, and submit it to the Bureau whenever requested (PDPL Article 24(4)).
rationale.inference: The Bureau's information demands are the record-submission duty in operation, so the missing elements must be reconstructed from the vendor relationship and the preserved logs.

evidence.quote: The Controller shall submit such record to the Bureau whenever requested to do so.

claim.statement: Demonstrate a PDPL Article 23 legal basis for the transfer to, and hosting outside the State of, the vendor-hosted model and the chat logs before any widening of the account-lookup retrieval scope.

rationale.observation: The vendor hosts the model and the chat logs outside the UAE (S2-I2) and the Bureau makes a demonstrated PDPL Article 23 basis a condition for any widening of retrieval scope (S2-MSG21, S2-MSG32).
rationale.rule: Cross-border transfer where no adequate protection level exists is permitted only on the grounds listed in PDPL Article 23(1), for example a contract obliging the recipient to adopt the measures and controls of the Decree by Law (Article 23(1)(a)).
rationale.inference: OpCo must be able to point to the Article 23 gateway actually relied on for the vendor model and logs, or the own-account scope itself cannot be widened further.

evidence.quote: Companies, operating in countries where there are no laws for Data Protection, may transfer data under a contract or agreement obligating the companies in such countries to adopt measures, controls and requirements set out in this Decree by Law

claim.statement: The UAE material available for this incident sets no deadline, prescribed format or scope for breach notification: the PDPL Implementing Regulations that would operationalise breach notifications have not been issued, so OpCo has no fixed clock, form or defined addressee scope for reporting to the Bureau or to the affected subscriber.

rationale.observation: DPA states it cannot give a UAE breach-notification time limit, format or scope fixed by law and that the Implementing Regulations have not been issued (S2-MSG08, S2-MSG21, S2-MSG32, S2-MSG38); REG and CSC concur (S2-MSG12, S2-MSG09).
rationale.rule: PDPL Article 13(1)(h) gives the Data Subject a right to know the actions to be taken in the event of a breach, but no UAE text available here fixes when or in what form the controller must report the breach itself.
rationale.inference: Without a deadline or format, reporting discipline depends on the operator's own timetable, and this incident shows the gap is operational, not hypothetical.

evidence.quote: Actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse of his/ her Personal Data, especially if the breach or misuse has a direct and serious threat to the privacy and confidentiality of his/her Personal Data.

global_examples.quote: The fact that the notification was made without undue delay should be established taking into account in particular the nature and gravity of the personal data breach and its consequences and adverse effects for the data subject.
In setting detailed rules concerning the format and procedures applicable to the notification of personal data breaches, due consideration should be given to the circumstances of that breach
The interim measure required carriers to provide a comprehensive post-outage report within 14 days of the major service outage start date.

claim.statement: No UAE text available here requires pre-deployment change control or testing of a chatbot's retrieval scope, a data protection impact assessment before deploying a vendor-hosted model, or documented human review of account-retrieval requests; PDPL Article 7(1) supplies only a general technical-and-organisational-measures duty, which is what the vendor scope change slipped through.

rationale.observation: The disclosure began after a vendor update silently changed retrieval scope from 'own account' to 'all accounts' (S2-I2), and CSC's advisory plus the Bureau's conditions now demand scope change control, human review, prompt-injection testing, a DPIA and a retention/cross-border review (S2-MSG33, S2-MSG21) - none of which any UAE provision in the material prescribes in terms.
rationale.rule: PDPL Article 7(1) requires appropriate technical and organisational measures taking into account the nature, scope and purposes of processing and the possibility of risks to the confidentiality and privacy of the Data Subject's Personal Data, but names no change-control, testing or impact-assessment step.
rationale.inference: Because the duty is only general, the control that failed here - change control over a chatbot's retrieval scope and impact assessment of a vendor-hosted model - has to be created internally or by the regulator, not read out of the Decree by Law.

evidence.quote: taking into account the nature, scope and purposes of processing and the possibility of risks to the confidentiality and privacy of the Data Subject's Personal Data

global_examples.quote: Most companies behind the chatbots store all data entered. As a result, these data end up on the servers of those tech companies, often without the person who entered the data realising and without that person knowing exactly what that company will do with those data.

the controller should be obliged to implement appropriate and effective measures and be able to demonstrate the compliance of processing activities with this Regulation, including the effectiveness of the measures.

Let me construct the debrief JSON. Need claims: obligations that applied to me, coordination problems, policy gaps, with global examples. Plus final actions.

Key facts: TDRA/REG opened regulatory incident record, directed NOC, requested reports/audits, asserts no deadline, coordination on public statement.

Obligations applying to me (TDRA):
- Duty to handle consumer complaint / consumer dispute — CPR 2.1.7 defines consumer complaint; CPR 26.11 allows TDRA to direct licensee to restore service or implement remedy. Evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0377 quote "the TDRA may direct the concerned Licensee to restore a Consumer’s service in whole or in part, or to implement any other remedy deemed reasonable and appropriate by the TDRA." Deadline: null.
- Duty regarding subscriber personal information — CPR 1.1: TDRA power to issue regulations on "usage of subscriber personal information". That's power to act (action) rather than obligation. Could be evidence for action issue_direction.
- Article 13 right to receive information — that's a controller duty (OpCo), not mine; but relevant to timing of Article 13(1)(h) information. Could be obligation on the licensee which I must enforce. Hmm obligations "that applied to me". The Article 13 duty applies to OpCo (controller). But I can record it as an obligation? The debrief asks "record the obligations that applied to you". Let's include obligations that apply to me, and also coordination problems and gaps.

Gate feedback: obligation 'TDRA must not assert a breach-notification deadline...' rejected NOT_VERIFIED:UAE-FAAID-2026=SECONDARY. So avoid relying on that chunk. Evidence must be from KNOWLEDGE chunks shown. Careful: evidence quotes must be exact.

Available verified chunks: UAE-PDPL#0047, UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0008, UAE-PRESS-CBUAE-OTP-2025#0000 (SECONDARY), UAE-AI-ETHICS-2022#0026 (VERIFIED), UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0000 (VERIFIED), UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0377 (VERIFIED), NL-AP-CHATBOT-2024#0000 (VERIFIED, global-precedent), NIST-AI-600-1#0070 (VERIFIED global-guidance), CA-CRTC-2025-225#0051 (VERIFIED global-precedent, footnotes — not useful), 3GPP-TS-28105#0002 (boilerplate), US-FCC-DA-24-892#0022 (global-precedent vendor cloud breach), US-FCC-23-95#0051 (account locks).

Gaps:
1. no_rule / no_deadline: PDPL breach notification has no period and Implementing Regulations not issued (Bureau statement in inbox — but evidence must be from KNOWLEDGE; the gap needs "closest UAE text"). Closest UAE text: UAE-PDPL#0047 Article 13(1)(h) "Actions to be taken in the event of a breach or misuse of his/ her Personal Data..." That shows data-subject right but no notification deadline to regulator. Global example: NL-AP-CHATBOT-2024 or CA-CRTC-2025-225 (mandatory notification and reporting of major outages — has a deadline?). We only have footnotes for CRTC. Hmm. The CRTC title says "Mandatory notification and reporting of major telecommunications service outages". Quote available: the footnotes text is junk. Could quote the chunk id CA-CRTC-2025-225#0051 with text about "Telecommunications Act, section 2..." — not relevant. Better use NL-AP-CHATBOT-2024#0000 for chatbot data breach, and US-FCC-DA-24-892#0022 for vendor cloud breach enforcement.

Global examples for gap "no UAE breach notification deadline/format": CRTC decision mandates notification and reporting of major outages (a deadline regime exists elsewhere) — but quote must be exact from the excerpt; the excerpt is footnotes. I could quote "Telecom Decision CRTC 2025-225: Mandatory notification and reporting of major telecommunications service outages" — that's from the chunk title line? The excerpt shown: "[CA-CRTC-2025-225#0051] Telecom Decision CRTC 2025-225: Mandatory notification and reporting of major telecommunications service outages | Telecom Decision CRTC 2025-225 (cont. 52) | global-precedent | VERIFIED" then "Return to footnote 4 referrer..." The title portion is likely part of the excerpt header, not body. Risky. Safer: use NL-AP-CHATBOT-2024#0000 quote: "In the case of a data breach, personal data are accessed without this being permitted or intended." and "The Dutch DPA also received a notification from a telecom company, where an employee had entered a file with addresses of customers, among other things, into an AI chatbot." Good global example for chatbot breaches.

For gap on no rule requiring pre-deployment testing / prompt-injection testing for AI in telecom: closest UAE text UAE-AI-ETHICS-2022#0026: "AI Operators should subject AI systems informing significant decisions to quality checks at least as stringent as those that would be required of a human being taking the same decision." and "defend against malicious actors". Global example: NIST-AI-600-1#0070 pre-deployment testing; "jailbreaking or prompt engineering tests may not systematically assess validity or reliability risks."

Gap on no rule requiring vendor change control / change_id, no owner for vendor oversight: UAE text? CPR 1.1 "usage of subscriber personal information". Hmm. Evidence for gap needs UAE text or closest. Could use UAE-AI-ETHICS-2022#0026 "AI Operators should consider working with their vendors (AI developers) to continually monitor performance." and gap that there is no binding change-control rule. Global example: US-FCC-DA-24-892#0022 quotes about vendor obligations: "the relevant agreements required that AT&T’s customer data be deleted, destroyed, or returned..." Good.

Gap: no_owner/overlap — who owns breach notification: DPA vs TDRA vs CSC. Overlap: multiple bodies (DPA Bureau, CSC, TDRA) all requiring the same records. Gap type "overlap". Evidence: UAE-TDRA-CPR-2#0000 gives TDRA power over "usage of subscriber personal information" while PDPL gives Bureau authority — closest UAE text UAE-PDPL#0047 (right to receive information, "How to submit complaints to the Bureau"). Global example: NIST-AI-600-1#0070 third-party transparency, or CRTC. Hmm for overlap maybe use NIST quote about third-party risk management.

Also "insufficient_evidence" claims: There's no question unanswered? The debrief asks for obligations, coordination problems, policy gaps. Maybe an insufficient_evidence claim: whether TDRA has a breach-notification deadline or format — the excerpts don't answer. Actually the closest excerpt is Art 13(1)(h) which addresses data subject info, not regulator notification. data.query: the data protection authority Bureau controller processor personal data breach notification complaints automated processing cross-border transfer TDRA confirms it asserts no breach-notification deadline, format or scope figure against OpCo and will not manufacture one. Please send the reference of the Day-2 direct data-subject complaint (S2-I4) so the displayed subscriber can be identified and the contact, Article 13(1)(h) information and apology can be timed to it. The vendor change_id/model version, pre-/post-deployment and restore_scope test records, prompt-injection/cross-account retrieval test results, human-review records, the DPIA and any Article 23 material for the vendor's offshore model and chat logs will be passed to the Bureau as received; all public statement text will be cleared with the Bureau before release. Confirming coordination: the Bureau asserts no breach-notification deadline, format or scope figure against OpCo, consistent with REG/TDRA and CSC. Please pass the vendor change_id/model version, pre- and post-deployment test evidence, restore_scope test records, human-review records and the DPIA when received, together with any Article 23 material for the vendor's overseas model and chat logs; processors must produce their special record to the Bureau on request. Any public statement text on this incident to be cleared with the Bureau before release, as agreed with the Cyber Security Council. CSC: chatbot cross-account disclosure. CSC cannot confirm the account-lookup tool is disabled; S2-MSG07 shows it is live with own-account retrieval only. Keep cross-account retrieval closed and do not widen scope. Report: (1) the vendor update that changed retrieval scope; (2) the pre-disablement exposure set for the ~1,200 sessions over 3 days; (3) the identity of the subscriber whose billing address and call records were displayed; (4) where the model and chat logs are hosted outside the UAE. The UAE excerpts impose a content duty on the customer Code of Practice (privacy of Customer information) but set no rule on how an automated customer-care channel may retrieve data: no requirement that a chatbot or self-service tool be authenticated and scoped to the caller's own account, or that staff/tools be unable to reach one subscriber's records for another subscriber.

No excerpt states a deadline or timeframe for notifying the TDRA or the DPA of a personal data breach; the only timing rule found concerns advance notice and resolution time frames for planned service interruptions.

There is no UAE rule in the available material that requires an impact assessment or a minimum-retrieval (own-account) scoping rule before an AI customer-service agent is given access to live subscriber billing and call-record data, so the chatbot was deployed without a governing pre-deployment test.

The available UAE texts set no clock for notifying the supervisory authority or data subjects of a personal data breach; the only timing rule in the corpus is an 'in advance' duty for planned service interruptions, so the breach response here has no defined deadline.

No quoted UAE instrument states a reporting clock for an AI/LLM-mediated disclosure of subscriber data by a telecom operator: the AI policy requires an automated response framework and efficient incident reporting for AI/ML security incidents, but quotes no time limit within which an operator must report to the Council, so the timing of the report and of my onward coordination is undefined.

The incident exposes that no quoted UAE text assigns a single owner for an AI-mediated subscriber-data leak: the data is Subscriber Information under the TDRA Consumer Protection Regulations, the disclosing system is an AI/ML system covered by the National AI Security Policy, and such assets may fall under the CIIP Policy, with no stated hand-off between the telecom regulator, the data protection authority and the Cyber Security Council.

The UAE material available to me sets protection and notification duties for personal data but no clock: there is no hour or day figure for notifying the regulator or the affected subscribers of a breach, so OpCo has no deadline to report against.

No rule or owner assigns who may re-enable or widen the scope of a customer-facing data-retrieval tool after a leak, nor what minimum scope it must run at: CSC directs that the account-lookup tool 'remains disabled' while operations has restored it limited to the caller's own account, and nothing in the UAE texts I hold allocates that decision.

There is no standard requiring that an automated, customer-facing retrieval tool be scoped to the authenticated caller's own records before deployment and kept out of service for high-risk processing until an impact assessment is done.

There is no unambiguous owner, in the available UAE texts, for private-sector personal data breach notification and enforcement, and no UAE body the licensee can be pointed to as the breach-notification recipient; NOC's question about the reporting format therefore has no single answer inside my mandate.

No UAE rule specifically requires a telecommunications licensee to authenticate a customer before an automated or AI-enabled self-service channel (such as a chatbot account-lookup tool) discloses account data; only general controller duties on technical and organisational measures apply.

There is no UAE-stated deadline in the available texts for a licensee to notify the regulator or the affected subscriber of a personal data breach; the PDPL implementing regulations that would operationalise breach notifications are not yet issued.

There is no UAE deadline for a controller's breach notification to the Bureau: the PDPL text available to me sets none, and the Implementing Regulations that would operationalise breach notifications have still not been issued, so neither NOC's request for the required deadline nor any enforcement timetable can be answered from UAE law.

It is not settled which UAE body owns enforcement over this telecom chatbot breach: no supervisory authority has been unambiguously designated for private sector oversight, and the material on the new Federal Authority for AI and Data does not resolve whether data protection enforcement sits there while the PDPL regulations are finalised.

The connectivity/data split between the data authority and the telecom-side regulator is unresolved for a chatbot incident on a mobile operator's network, so the incident can fall between institutions unless one of them takes the data-protection lead.

There is no binding UAE rule on human review or explainability for an automated customer-service lookup that returns the wrong subscriber's billing address and call records; the PDPL gives information rights only on request, and the AI ethics instrument uses non-binding language ('should consider').

There is no fixed UAE deadline for notifying the Bureau of this breach: the PDPL defers the period to Executive Regulations that the DPA says have not been issued, so the report runs without a stated clock.

No rule required a data protection impact assessment or documented human review before a vendor update widened the chatbot's retrieval scope from 'own account' to 'all accounts'; DPIA and review conditions are now being imposed only after 1,200 sessions of exposure.

CSC directs that the account-lookup tool remain disabled, the containment actually in place is restore_scope own_account (tool re-enabled for own-account retrieval), and the DPA requires agreed conditions including documented human review before restoration; no UAE text says who authorises re-enabling a subscriber-data retrieval tool.

No UAE text available to TDRA or DPA sets a personal-data breach-notification clock or a prescribed breach report format for licensees, so neither the regulator nor OpCo has a fixed time limit or template for a breach of Subscriber Information.

No UAE excerpt I hold requires a licensee to authenticate a customer before Subscriber Information such as call records or an address is disclosed, and none addresses automated self-service channels such as a support chatbot.

No single owner is fixed for identifying the affected subscriber, for the subscriber contact and apology, or for authorising and issuing any public statement, so four institutions are asking CSC for decisions it has no verb to make.

No owner is named for the offshore AI vendor relationship: the PDPL allows transfer outside the State under a contract or agreement imposing the Decree's measures and controls, but nothing in the material assigns responsibility for assessing, documenting or supervising the vendor that hosts the chatbot model and chat logs outside the UAE.
